audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows contradict the packet, the mirror, and the page's own whys.
audit.why: whys[0] says you have no root and no answer at level 1 — that is a Jayce row, not Skill. whys[4] ends 'the extended fight is now yours' and whys[5] ends 'the poke war is over', both under rows credited to Skill or Jayce, and whys[6] calls you unkillable in a teamfight under a Jayce row. The packet reads Jayce, Jayce, Jayce, Skill, Swain, Skill, Swain and the mirror set the same.
audit.corrected: win[0]/phases[0].side to Jayce; win[4]/phases[4].side and win[6]/phases[6].side to Swain; win[5]/phases[5].side to Skill.

audit.why: Spike shape is right — his levels 1-3, your level 6, your first item, a grouped late game — and the level 6 drain window is correctly identified as the pivot.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] has him firing Shock Blast through an Acceleration Gate at Level 1, and nothing anywhere mentions what his stance swap does to your resistances.
audit.why: Gate and Shock Blast are both the cannon form of two different slots — he cannot have the Gate at level 1, so the level 1 warning describes a combo that does not exist yet, while the real level 1 problem (his raw range against your 750 Q) goes unsaid. Separately, Riot's text says the first attack after swapping to Mercury Cannon reduces the target's Armor AND Magic Resist — on a page whose whole tldr is 'build MR', that is the interaction that decides whether the MR is there when it matters.
audit.corrected: Level 1 restated without the impossible Gate combo; the swap's resistance shred and its auto-reset tell written into mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid gives Shock Blast 'roughly a ten-second cooldown'.
audit.why: It runs 16/14/12/10/8/6 — 16 seconds early, and 6 when maxed. Counting ten all game means stepping up into a live Shock Blast in the late levels and giving up free windows in the early ones.
audit.corrected: Real range written in with the trade rule keyed to it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The knockback is described as interrupting your root.
audit.why: Thundering Blow knocks you back; the root comes off Nevermove's return pass and is not interrupted by it. What the knockback really costs you is the 650 drain radius, and it is on 20 seconds at rank 1, so he only gets one per fight.

edits.before: Jayce fires Shock Blast through a Gate from outside your E range at Level 1 — you have no root and no answer; farm at maximum Q distance and accept the early poke.
edits.after: At Level 1 he has no Gate yet, but Shock Blast still reaches past everything you own and you have no root to answer it — farm at max Q distance and accept the poke.

edits.before: Jayce's Shock Blast (Q) through an Acceleration Gate chunks you from beyond E range before your root is ever a threat — these levels are entirely his.
edits.after: Once Acceleration Gate is up, a Shock Blast fired through it chunks you from well beyond your 850 E before the root is ever a threat — these levels are his.

edits.before: Use the Knockback (hammer E) to interrupt your root or push you out of R drain range the moment you activate Demonic Ascension
edits.after: Thundering Blow you out of the 650 drain range the moment Demonic Ascension starts — 20 seconds at rank 1, so he gets one

edits.before: From Levels 4 through 6 the lane is a cooldown chess match. Shock Blast has roughly a ten-second cooldown — count it after every poke, and that window is your entire agency. When it is down, step up and threaten W; if he swaps into hammer to contest, that is the moment to E-root, pull with passive, and dump Q bolts. When Shock Blast is up, give nothing and farm. At Level 6 the math tilts meaningfully in your favor: activate R the moment he commits a hammer-stance all-in, because Demonic Ascension heals through his burst and every second you drain is a Soul Fragment adding permanent max HP. Jayce cannot out-damage sustained R healing in an extended fight, so his only answer is to knock you back with hammer E and disengage — predict that knockback and angle your position so it shoves you toward your minions rather than his tower.
edits.after: From Levels 4 through 6 the lane is a cooldown chess match. Shock Blast runs 16 seconds early and only reaches 6 when maxed — count it after every poke, because that window is your entire agency. When it is down, step up and threaten W; if he swaps to hammer to contest, throw E past him so the return pass roots, pull, and dump Q bolts. Watch the swap itself: it resets his attack and the first hit in cannon form shreds your armour and magic resist, so the MR you bought is thinnest exactly when he opens. At 6 the maths tilts to you — R his hammer all-in, drain through the burst, bank fragments. His only answer is Thundering Blow, so stand where the knockback throws you toward your own minions.

notes: whys[0] warned about a Level 1 Shock Blast fired through an Acceleration Gate; he cannot have the Gate at level 1, so the page's opening advice described an impossible combo while leaving the real level 1 problem unstated. Shock Blast's cooldown was given as 'roughly ten seconds' — it is 16 down to 6, which changes the count at both ends of the game. Added the interaction that matters most on a page built around building magic resist: swapping to Mercury Cannon resets his attack and that first hit reduces armour and MR, so the resistances are lowest at the exact moment his combo starts. Four chart rows flipped in matched pairs to the packet and mirror; whys[4] and whys[5] declare the fight yours and the poke war over under rows the chart gave away.
